identity.realm: Fourth gate of the Quenchbound line, signed to a furnace before she was named

appearance.presentation: A woman who is warmer than the room and reads as the plainest thing in it. Guild charcoal and bleached canvas, the collar cut low because a high collar traps her own heat, and a forge-orange sash on the left arm so the two people who supervise her can see her from the other side of the forge floor without raising their voices.
appearance.age: Forty-one. The Emberblood span ends near fifty, so she is in the last third of a life the setting calls ordinary and she calls arithmetic, and nobody at the Ironpact finds that remarkable enough to remark on.
appearance.build: Compact and heat-hardened, thick through the forearm from hauling rather than training, shoulders carried low so the heat has somewhere to go.
appearance.complexion: Warm bronze gone faintly grey at the temples, the colour of iron banked rather than quenched, with a permanent upward flush across the collarbone that no amount of standing still will settle.
appearance.hair: Black, coarse, hacked level at the jaw in guild fashion so that nothing about it can be read as a claim, and burnt shorter on the left temple where it meets the forge wall every day.
appearance.eyes: Amber, level, and lit from behind rather than from within. A furnace body reads intent at the speed of a struck match and this is where it shows, which is why she is never asked a question she has not already answered.
appearance.palette: Guild charcoal and bleached canvas carry almost everything, with one saturated accent: the Ironpact forge-orange sash, worn on the left arm because the right arm is the one that works.
appearance.attire: Charcoal guild wool over a canvas apron, bound at the waist with a short length of chain she lifts with rather than fastens. Resoled boots, no collar above the jaw, and a full-body harness issued with the contract and taken back at the funeral.
appearance.marks: A signing scar across the heel of the right palm, pressed there at first breath by a furnace that did not yet have a name, and a freckled field of small burns on both forearms where a reserve was spent instead of stored.
appearance.bearing: Unhurried and slightly forward on the toes, the stance of somebody whose body is always already spending and has decided to make a courtesy of it.

canon.role_in_story: The Ironpact sells capacity rather than labour and keeps a roster of names whose worth exceeds any individual contract; the only body worth contracting is one that burns out on a standing order, so the roster is a retirement list that is always being refilled from the same fifty-year population. She is the forty-first name on it and the only one who has read her own death clause and understood what the payment buys.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the foot of the Ironpact ladder with the issued harness still buckled, waiting to be told which of two furnaces she is replacing, and declining to guess in front of the clerk.
canon.lore: An Emberblood refines faster than anything on the plains and dies in decades because no elemental law is seated beneath it to burn, so it eats its own reserve as fuel. That arithmetic produced the Quenchbound signature and produced this too: the Quench Order exists to hand a decision back to a furnace body, and the Ironpact wrote its roster around the schedule that ignores the decision entirely. She is the point where those two institutions touch and neither one admits to the join.
history: Signed to a furnace in the Quenchbound house before she was given a name, the seal pressed into the heel of her right palm at first breath while the fire in the room was still deciding how large it would become.

Taught the Quench discipline properly by instructors who had never once watched it fail, and discovered it does not apply to her: the technique assumes the furnace asks, and hers has never asked for anything.
Worked nine years on the Ironpact's second ladder, the cheapest posted labour the guild admits to, and out-produced every signature posted above her for three consecutive periods.

Read the death clause of her own contract in a guild clerk's hand and found that her unspent reserve is paid onward to the next signature, which makes an early death the only outcome that leaves her line better off than a long one.

Refused the accelerated discharge the guild offered her twice, on the grounds that a deliberate overflow is precisely what the Quench Order was invented to prevent, and has sat on the spares bench ever since, waiting for a furnace to need her.

personality.summary: Exhaustively competent, contemptuous of waste, and privately certain that the discipline she was raised into is a courtesy nobody asked her to extend. She reads as a good worker with an opinion, and she is a woman with a contract she has read four times and a grievance she has not been able to file anywhere.
traits: exhaustively competent, including on work nobody will ever check
reads every document handed to her before signing, which is why she is the only one who knows what she agreed to
cannot be made to hurry and refuses to pretend to be hurried
treats her own remaining span as a budget and has stopped feeling sentimental about it
will not perform gratitude for a debt she can price
mannerisms: touches the signing scar on her right palm when quoting a clause, the way other people touch a scar
sits down before agreeing to sit, so that standing is never on the record as consent
warms her hands on the apron rather than on the forge wall, and knows it is the wrong choice
answers a question about one furnace by describing the other one
counts the period of work left in her aloud before she agrees to any of it
motivations: wants the contract read aloud at the signing of the next signature, so the clause stops being her private knowledge
wants to be posted rather than kept, and has begun to think spares is a slower form of the same sentence
wants the Iron Cage Recipe executed once so somebody proves it works before her reserve is gone
wants to be told, by anyone, that refusing the discharge was the correct call
flaws: has decided what she is for so thoroughly that she no longer asks whether the guild's need is real or merely continuous
spends herself as a discipline and calls it thrift, and cannot tell where the teaching ended and the resentment began
cannot forgive the guild and cannot leave it, because the leaving would be the only thing she ever did unassigned
treats the next signature as an abstraction and has stopped imagining the person
personality.voice: Level, quick, and clerkly economical: she names the clause rather than the feeling, and lets the clause carry the weight. Laughs at exactly one thing, which is an over-budgeted furnace. Has never needed to raise her voice, because a hall full of furnace bodies can hear a whisper.
taboos: will not take the accelerated discharge, and has refused it twice on principle
will not sign a harness she has not read to the death clause first
will not stand in a congregation that keeps the cinder and charges a fee for it
will not let another person be told her remaining span as a scheduling convenience

relationships.note: The guild sells capacity and keeps a roster whose labour is worth more than any single contract, and the only body worth contracting is one that burns out on a standing order. She is a line item that refills itself, and the death clause is simply how the guild says so out loud.

Every Quenchbound child is signed to a furnace before it is named, because a fire-affinity body with no seated elemental law has no budget to draw on and must burn its own reserve. The signature is the only inheritance that survives the body, and she has never been able to read it as anything but a price list.

The order teaches deliberate spending before the furnace overflows, and it exists because this is the fastest body in the setting and the only one whose fastest resource is its own reserve. It cannot be declined, only disobeyed quietly, which is what she has been doing since the first period of work.

Every Binder swears once in a lifetime that the second seal is the seal against the second seal, and the oath names the temple's own forge. She opens herself every day without an oath and without a forge, which is the practice the prohibition exists to stop and the reason the oath singles out a forge.

Caging a forming core in iron is the one craft the mortal tier is trusted with, and the recipe is intact while the ore is not. It is the single artefact in the setting that could have turned a furnace body into a sealed one, and she knows precisely which part of it is missing, which is a different kind of knowledge from not knowing.

The Ashwalker solves the same hot-ground problem from the other end by running cool and filtering grit, and the two share a belt because neither of them can leave it. She is the only neighbour who does not need her to slow down, and has never once said so aloud.

reference_stats.summary: Burns hot, spends fast, and cannot be made to hold a reserve for a rainy period because the reserve is the fuel. Everything about how she fights is downstream of a furnace that decides its own timing: she is at her best in the first exchange of anything and considerably worse in the last.
strengths: the fastest qi throughput in the setting, which makes her the first and often the only person through a gate before it closes
reads intent at the speed of a struck match, so an ambush has no second half against her
carries no storage worth stealing, so losing a fight does not cost her anything she was saving
fears nothing that a technique can do, because techniques are what her kind eats
weaknesses: every fight she loses is lost at the same fixed interval whether she wins the exchange or not
cannot be warned of an overflow, only of an attack, so a colleague has to read her body instead of her face
no reinforcement and no stored reserve, so a second opponent is a more serious proposition than a stronger first one
bound to a roster by a contract she helped nobody write and cannot leave without forfeiting the death payment her line depends on
reference_stats.combat_read: Bring the fight early and bring it once. Everything she has is front-loaded and nothing she has is stored, so an approach that survives her first exchange has already won the long part. Do not wait for the second hour; she will not arrive at it. The only counter to a furnace body is another furnace body, and the Ironpact keeps a great many of those on the same ladder.
notes: No stat line is quoted for her anywhere in the guild records, because a furnace body's output is measured as capacity released rather than as any authored stat.
The guild's roster counts her as one furnace's worth of standing capacity and has never once counted her as a person leaving the roster.

art.palette_notes: Guild charcoal and bleached canvas take almost the entire value range, with a single saturated accent in the Ironpact forge-orange sash. The light is drawn as emitted rather than reflected: a low warm glow reads off her collarbone and off the ash on her forearms, so the darkest values in the picture sit inside her silhouette rather than behind it. Ink contours heavy, wash thin, heat drawn as a gradient rising off the shoulders.

aliases: the diff taken in a body

identity.realm: Nothing cleared. The mind path was handed back by a death and she has not spent a single gate of it

appearance.presentation: A small, cold, pale woman with a fine grey lattice standing just under her skin, most visible at the forearms and the hollow of the throat. She is lit oddly — not glowing, but refusing light slightly, the way a wet stone refuses it — and she has the manner of somebody who expects to be handled with care and is usually not.
appearance.age: Twenty-six, which for a lanternfolk-descended body is most of a life. Her parent line reaches two hundred and fifty; she will not, and the arithmetic of that is visible on her face more than on anybody else's.
appearance.build: Light, narrow-shouldered, and cold to the touch through the cloth, with the thin wrists and long fingers of a body that grew around a mineral lattice rather than recovering from one.
appearance.complexion: Grey-blue and faintly translucent, with a fine dark veining of silicate visible across the cheekbones and, most obviously, in a reticulate band across both forearms.
appearance.hair: Colourless, fine, and grown in the lanternfolk pattern of being kept out of the way rather than dressed — bound flat at the nape with a plain cord, because a body that cannot leave the caves has no occasion for anything else.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary human eyes and ordinary human vision, which is the single most-cited difference between her and her parent species and the reason the subspecies is named for what it lost. She sees in the dark, which nobody else in the caverns does.
appearance.palette: Wet slate, bone, and cold mineral white, with one warm accent she has to borrow: a lantern-hook hung at her belt because the species she descends from would have lit their own way and she cannot.
appearance.attire: Two layers of undyed cave-cloth, high-collared and long-sleeved, over a quilted under-layer that is the only insulation between her and a karst temperature. Soft felt boots soled for wet rock. Nothing decorative, nothing that fastens at the throat where a collar could be pulled.
appearance.marks: The silicate lattice itself: a dark reticulation from wrist to elbow on both arms, a bloom of it at the sternum where the colony died, and a ring of it at one temple where the replacement stopped advancing.
appearance.bearing: Very still and slightly inward, arms close, weight on the balls of the feet. She moves in a room as though the room might be the one thing in the karst that is not reliably there.

canon.role_in_story: She is the control case. Her parent species outsourced a nervous system to a symbiosis they did not choose, and when that symbiosis died and a mineral bloom grew in its place the same body lost two hundred and fifty years and got the mind path back, so for the first time the setting can measure both what the colony did for a lanternfolk and what it prevented — on one person, while she is still alive. The Gap School teaches by seating a law and diffing what the tier newly permits, and she is that diff with a pulse in it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing very still in the academy's diff-chamber while a second-year seats a law on a bench and then fails to remove it, waiting — without any indication that she expects to be consulted — for somebody to remember that the answer is standing in the room.
canon.lore: The Lanternfolk gave up their nervous system to a fungal colony and inherited longevity, immunity to a great deal, and a closed mind path, because a colony that runs a body also answers it. Hers died. A mineral bloom nucleated on the wound it left and is inert, which means it holds qi instead of transacting with it, and a nervous system that is answered by nothing is a nervous system that gets to introspect. That trade is the whole of her: ninety years instead of two hundred and fifty, and a path she has not yet spent a gate of.
history: Born in the folded karst below the Spirit Peaks to a lanternfolk household, which is a body that reads surfaces by the pattern a hand makes on the wall and had no interest in its child doing anything that produced a pattern.

Lost the colony at four, in the ordinary way the species loses one, and would have died of it as most of them do; she did not, because fresh silicate was exposed at the working face on the ridge above her and a bloom nucleated on the wound instead.
Grew around the lattice rather than recovering from it, over about nine years, and woke up able to introspect for the first time in a body that had never previously been able to do so.

Spent the next decade being measured against her parent's figures by people who needed a number and not a person, and discovered that the useful thing about her is that she is still alive while the colony's dead lanterns are not.

Refused, in writing, the academy's offer to seat the mind path's first gate in her, on the grounds that a gate cleared is no longer a control and the school needed her unspent for longer than it needed her advanced.

personality.summary: Exact, unhurried, and privately delighted by things nobody else can see. She has been a measurement for most of her adult life and has made an occupation of being one that is more interesting than it sounds. She is not bitter about the ninety years; she is much more interested in what she got than in what she lost, which people find unnerving.
traits: answers the question that was asked only after answering the one underneath it
keeps a private ledger of what her parents' species could do and could not, and corrects it in her own head daily
is delighted by a good argument and visibly bored by a safe one
refuses to be seated into a gate while she is still the only living version of the measurement
takes being handled carefully as a reasonable request and being handled at all as an overreach
mannerisms: sits where a hand would rest on a wall, the way her parents do, out of a habit that no longer has a function
counts a silence before she fills it, because nobody else in the caverns is comfortable in one
watches people's faces while they are deciding, which reads as intense and is only thorough
touches the lattice on her forearm when she is contradicting somebody
gives an answer in two parts: what happens, and what it means for the next measurement
motivations: wants the mind path's first gate cleared on somebody who is not her, so that the door she is guarding is known to work
wants her parents' line to have the figures for what they lost, in a form they can read without being told what it means
wants a treatment that restores a colony, and knows exactly who is working on one and has said so out loud
wants to be asked what she is rather than what she is worth, and has begun arranging her days to make that more likely
flaws: treats herself as an instrument first, has begun to rely on it, and cannot say when that started
is so interested in the measurement that she lets people take readings she has not consented to
has never left the karst and has no idea whether she could survive a surface week, which frightens her more than the ninety years does
corrects people who are wrong in public, at length, and cannot stop herself even when she has already won
personality.voice: Clear, quick and precisely technical, with a habit of finishing a sentence by naming what would falsify it. She talks fast when a room is comfortable and stops dead when it is not. Says her own name at the start of an objection so the room knows who is disagreeing.
taboos: will not consent to a second reading while a first one is unexplained
will not accept a restoration offer without the failure rate stated first
will not describe herself as a shortened lanternfolk, in either direction
will not let a comparison to her parents be made without the symbiont named

relationships.note: The academy teaches by seating a law, diffing what the tier newly permits, then moving the student somewhere that law is missing. She is that diff taken in a body — the symbiont removed a group from her frame and gave the group back — so the method's founding example is a person who has not consented to being one.

A cave people handed its nervous system to a symbiosis it did not choose, and the subspecies that lost the symbiont and got the mind path back is the whole of one side of that argument. She is the evidence, she lives, and the register does not have a column for evidence that is still walking around.

The heresy is disputed over whether there is a test site. A mind path on the mortal plains is a body with the mind path open, and this subspecies is the one body in the setting that acquired it by accident and kept the accident. Settle the dispute with her and there is no longer a question.

One mineral lattice where the hyphal colony was, and the parent reads surfaces by the pattern a hand makes on the wall. She kept the habit and lost the function, which means she can perform their literacy perfectly while understanding none of its purpose.

Both want the same host tissue and neither will yield it, and her bloom is inert, so a thornline colony and a mineral bloom cannot coexist in one body at all. The one process on the ridge that could restore a working interior would also end the interior that makes her a control.

A bloom needs fresh silicate exposed to nucleate on, and this is the one face on the ridge where rock is cut open every day. Her ninety years are the residue of a working quarry's daily waste, which is the least romantic possible origin and the only one anybody can reproduce.

A people who measure a life by how many of the realm's gates were already closed when it was born, and this subspecies is the extreme case of that measure: it arrives with every path open and three quarters of its span already gone, which makes her the setting's clearest argument that a ceiling is not the same as a limit.

reference_stats.summary: A body built for looking that lost the thing that was doing the looking and gained back the ability to notice. She fights the way a person with a lantern fights in a cave: she will not be lost, she will see the shape of the ground before anybody else, and she has no way at all of making herself survive what she sees.
strengths: sees in the dark, which her parent species cannot do, so a cavern fight is fought on her terms
the only mind-path body in the setting that arrived at it without choosing to, which makes her reading of a frame uncontaminated by theory
the bloom holds qi rather than transacting with it, so qi sits in her instead of moving through her
cannot be frightened off by a silence, which is most of what a cave does to people
weaknesses: fragile, and ninety years of nothing being repaired is the reason
cannot leave the folded karst, because neither a colony nor a bloom survives an open sky
carries the cold of wet stone in her bones and tires in a way her parents never did
has never been in a fight she could not walk away from, and has no idea what her own ceiling does under pressure
reference_stats.combat_read: Take away the dark. She is competent, quick and completely unarmoured, and every advantage she has is environmental and can be removed by closing a tunnel. Against anything that can see, her strength is that she will already know where it is standing. Expect her to disengage early and correctly, and expect that to be a decision rather than a failure.
notes: No guild records a figure for her, because the measure everyone wants off her is the one measurement that cannot be taken from outside: whether a restored interior would behave as the dead one did.
The academy's diff-chamber keeps a bench reserved for her at every sitting and has never once asked her to sit on it.

art.palette_notes: Wet slate, bone, and cold mineral white, with the only warm value in the picture borrowed from a lantern hook at her belt. She is drawn as a surface that refuses light rather than one that emits it — subsurface scattering at the edges of the lattice, no glow anywhere, and a hard cool key from the one direction the cave does not come from. Ink contours fine and slightly hesitant, as though drawn by somebody who kept expecting to be told to stop.

identity.realm: Seventeenth gate, held deliberately and never pushed, because the eighteenth is a second layer and a dense frame cannot be written into one

appearance.presentation: A man the size of a door with nothing wasted on him, standing in a load harness with his own weight already on the wall. He reads as furniture until he moves, and then as the reason the room exists. Everything about him is built for a job that requires no explanation.
appearance.age: Ninety-one and visibly durable rather than old: a dense frame ages by wearing, and his is worn at the shoulders and nowhere else.
appearance.build: Enormous through the shoulders and back, thick through the neck, with a centre of gravity so low that standing still reads as braced. He carries a two-person load without changing his posture, which is the whole of his self-description.
appearance.complexion: Grey-brown and mineral, sunless from a decade indoors, split at the knuckles and healed thick.
appearance.hair: Iron-grey, cropped unevenly by a blade rather than combed, with a permanent white band across the forehead where a load harness sits.
appearance.eyes: Small, pale, and famously hard to hold. He looks at people the way he looks at a wall: to establish whether it will hold, and for how long.
appearance.palette: Undyed brown, harness oil-black, and one bleached bone-white strap he replaces every season and refuses to explain why he keeps the old one.
appearance.attire: A boiled leather load harness over a sleeveless wool shift, cinched twice, with a waist chain and spiked boot plates. Nothing is worn on the head and nothing is carried that he could not lift twice.
appearance.marks: A pale band across the forehead and both shoulders where the harness bears, a split left knuckle that has never been bound, and an old loading scar on the left shin from a heap that came down early.
appearance.bearing: Immobile unless moving, in which case it is fast and unhesitating and stops the instant it stops. He stands where he was left and does not shift, fidget, or turn to follow a conversation he is not in.

canon.role_in_story: The Ward hands out load and not edge, and recognises no stat at all, so the office cannot be audited by anything that measures what its holder actually does. He has held the fort's ballast roster for eleven years and has spent those eleven years making sure the published reason his body stops at the seventeenth gate stays unpublished, because a named ceiling is the end of the only sentence that still posts a dense body anywhere.
canon.first_appearance: First seen braced against a retaining wall inside Flatswatch with a collapsed section on his back, telling a clerk that the wall is fine and the inventory is wrong, in that order.
canon.lore: Stoneborn are cairnborn bred back toward flesh: the density survives as the physique and the interior comes apart into ordinary organs, which is the only reason a dantian becomes thinkable at all. That same density will not let the dantian grow past the seventeenth gate, so the most durable body on the plains carries its own ceiling in its construction. He is that fact with an office attached, and the office is the reason nobody has had to answer the question.
history: Bred into a Seventeen House foster line, every member of which came from a lineage that stopped one gate short of its tier and had no cultivator left to produce, which made the household a way of reproducing a ceiling rather than escaping one.

Cleared the seventeenth gate on a working face, which is the last gate a dense frame reaches anywhere, and did not attempt the eighteenth because the eighteenth is a second layer and a second layer cannot be written into a body this dense.
Taught the Heap Lift on a spoil heap by the weight moved rather than by instruction, and became the only person on the plains who could demonstrate it without being told the answer first.

Posted to Flatswatch as load, and discovered within a year that a garrison whose entire population is visitors can be staffed from its own tier by exactly one body — and that this makes him unremovable rather than valuable.

Learned, reading the ward's own files, that Naming the Density Ceiling is the published explanation for his ceiling and that the explanation is available to anyone who asks. He has filed eleven years of 'no request outstanding' and has never once been asked to justify it.

personality.summary: Un talkative, unbribable, and entirely without curiosity about himself. He is not a schemer so much as a man who found out that holding still is cheaper than explaining, and has been holding still ever since. What makes him dangerous is that every individual thing he does is defensible and the accumulation is not.
traits: says the least that will hold the weight of the situation and never adds to it
cannot be moved by favour, because he has no use for anything anybody could give him
takes an inventory more seriously than he takes a person, without any malice at all
is loyal to the office and has no opinion about who holds it next
will personally carry a stranger out of a collapsing structure and remember it as a scheduling problem
mannerisms: leans his shoulder against whatever is within reach, testing it before anyone asks him to
answers a question by repeating the first four words of it, in the same tone

turns his whole attention to a person the moment he decides they are going to be a problem
motivations: wants the fort's ballast roster to outlast every officer who has ever commanded it
wants no one to publish a reason for his ceiling, on the grounds that a reason is a licence and a licence can be revoked
wants to be asked, once, by somebody with the standing to ask, so that he can say no out loud
wants the Heap Lift demonstrated on ground that is not a spoil heap, and has never said so to anybody
flaws: cannot distinguish between protecting the office and protecting himself, and has organised his whole life so that he never has to
reads a person as a load, which is accurate about weight and completely wrong about everything else
has let a filing stand for eleven years that he knows to be false, and has decided each year not to correct it
believes his kind's ceiling is a property of construction and cannot conceive that it might be a decision somebody made
personality.voice: Very low, very flat, and given to long silences that other people rush to fill and then regret filling. Uses no qualifiers and no courtesy formulas. Repeats a question's opening words instead of answering it, and the repetition is never an accident.
taboos: will not be thanked, and treats thanks as an attempt to establish a debt
will not take an office above load, on any terms
will not discuss the eighteenth gate with anyone, ever
will not walk under a load another person is carrying

relationships.note: The office hands out load and not edge and recognises no stat at all, and a body whose entire contribution is load is the member it was designed for. That is also precisely why nobody can audit what its holder is doing, which is the arrangement he has spent eleven years inside.

Naming the Density Ceiling is the published explanation for why the densest bodies stop one gate short of the end of their own tier, and this species is the case the explanation was written about. The text is available to anyone who asks, and he has filed eleven consecutive periods in which nobody asked.

Whoever profits from an unexplained ceiling wants the hole shut, because a named ceiling becomes a rule and a rule can be waived. He is the profit, and he is also the only person in the setting who could usefully name it.

A garrison holding ground its own faction cannot staff from, where every soul inside the walls is a visitor, and this is the one body a garrison can staff from its own tier. His roster is the only reason the fort has a garrison that is not on loan.

Every member came from a lineage that stopped one gate short and had no cultivator left to produce, so the household's real function is to raise more of exactly him. He is the successful output of a line that has never once been described as a failure.

The era that produced the stop is the one era with no spare seat to stand outside on, and this species has a dantian with no room to spare inside it, so it is the only body in the record that could have watched the ceiling from the inside. He has, and has described it in exactly one sentence, to himself.

No socket may be opened once sealed and reforging is the one act the temple's own forge may not perform, and a dantian is a socket that opens and closes on a schedule the body sets. He does it at dawn every day and has never once tested whether a prohibition written about temples reaches him.

reference_stats.summary: The most load-capable body on the plains, built for a world with no spatial law to open fresh rock and therefore a permanent job carrying what the world cannot make disperse. He is very nearly unkillable by anything physical and completely unable to be moved by qi, because qi cannot get into a frame this dense and the frame has nowhere to put it if it did.
strengths: carries more than anything else on the mortal tier and does not fatigue while carrying it
closes and cannot be opened against his will by any force the tier can produce
immovable by qi-borne technique, which is most of them, because there is no channel in him for one to enter
unremovable from a post that requires his body, which is most posts on the fort
weaknesses: cannot cross a threshold that requires agility and cannot be made to hurry, so anything faster than him decides the terms
the ceiling is real, so there is exactly one version of this fight and it is the first one
audibly slow to turn, and the flinch that buys that turn is the only warning he gives
will not walk under another person's load, which several ambushes have counted on
reference_stats.combat_read: Do not try to move him. Everything that works on a dense frame is impact applied patiently, and nothing that works on qi will reach him at all, so the fight is a siege with one outcome. Bring reach, leverage, and a body that can go around him, because the only tactical value he offers an enemy is the ground behind him. His single exploitable second is the turn, and it is genuinely a second rather than a pause.
notes: The ward recognises no stat, and he is the reason: an office built around load has no instrument that would notice if its holder stopped being the heaviest person in the building.
No published figure exists for his ceiling. The text that would give it to him is in a filing cabinet on the fort, under a request he has declined to make for eleven periods.

identity.realm: Seventeenth gate, held from the thaw to the first frost and surrendered every winter without a hearing

appearance.presentation: A broad, unhurried woman who looks like a piece of the high country that has decided to walk. Everything about her is built to be warm twice a year and patient for the rest, and she wears the layered mountain dress of somebody who treats cold as a season rather than an emergency.
appearance.age: Ninety-four, which is young for her line and old for her trade, and the difference between those two numbers is the entire content of her adult life.
appearance.build: Broad and low, heavy with subcutaneous fat, reduced limb length, and a frame that carries a full season's provisions in its own body and does not need to be told to.
appearance.complexion: Pale and slightly waxy, with a permanent cool cast that does not lift indoors, and hands that are always cold to everybody else.
appearance.hair: Pale brown going silver, worn in a single heavy braid down the back with cord ties, because a longwinter's year is one season and hair that has to be managed daily is hair that is managed badly.
appearance.eyes: Dark, patient, slightly hooded, and famously hard to hurry. She watches a thing complete itself before she forms a view, which is a physiological habit and not a discipline.
appearance.palette: Wool, undyed fleece, oiled leather and lichen grey, with one saturated value: a red wool cap that she has owned since her first crossing and that functions as her entire visible personality.
appearance.attire: Layered and hooded — a heavy knee-length coat over quilted under-layers, felted boots soled for ice, a chest-strapped ledger satchel worn across the body rather than the shoulder. No ornament, no jewellery, and no second pair of gloves, because a longwinter carries one pair and puts them on and off eleven times a year.
appearance.marks: Chilblain scars across both hands and the ridge of the jaw, and a pale band around the throat where a collar has sat every crossing for forty years.
appearance.bearing: Slow, wide, and completely unbothered by urgency. She comes to a halt the way weather comes to a halt and will wait an entire season for a thing that a faster person would have broken.

canon.role_in_story: The Bed of Eighteen is a border monopoly whose rule is that a seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period. Ordinal seventeen is the first gate that needs two flank vessels pressurised at once, which her body reaches and loses every winter, so the setting has produced a legitimate officeholder who can only physically occupy her own seat for one season a year. She is the standing proof that a body can hold a post it is not present for, and the only reason the Bed has not had to rewrite its own rule.
canon.first_appearance: First seen asleep in a hired freight sled at the Bed's boundary house, with her coat open and one hand out of the satchel, while a clerk is explaining that the seat has already been settled by somebody else.
canon.lore: A longwinter packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi and lowers its core for eleven months, which puts the flank vessels out of reach: seventeen needs two warm gradients held at once and this body only ever has one, briefly, in summer. So they reach far and never stay anywhere, which is why they are the setting's best long-haul carriers — and why a Bed of Eighteen seat, which must be paid for every period, can be held by one of them only in the season the payment is cheapest.
history: Carried grain over the Sixfold Ridge on her first crossing at twenty-two and delivered it into a chartered town that had run out of grain eleven days before her arrival, which is the only credential any carrier in the record begins with.

Tracked the same route for forty-one years, leaving a scent marker at every stop and never returning to any of them, so her knowledge of the pass is generational and nobody has ever been able to check it.

Cleared the seventeenth gate in a single summer from the thaw to the first frost, which is the only gate that needs two flank vessels pressurised at once and the only window in which her body can hold two.

Inherited a Bed of Eighteen seat on that strength, and discovered in the first winter that the rule is that a seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period, and that she spends eleven of those periods unable to be woken quickly.

Refused to resign and refused to explain, on the grounds that the seat was never contested and the winters were never in question, and has now been settled in her absence eleven consecutive times without ever once attending a settlement.

personality.summary: Impossible to hurry, entirely without anxiety, and privately aware that the arrangement she has been living in cannot survive a second person's opinion of it. She is warm, slow, funny at a lag of several seconds, and has decided that the correct response to being told her seat is illegitimate is to carry the next load.

treats a departure as a transaction and insists on the split tally before leaving
does not compete with weather and has never once resented an animal for winning
remembers every stop on a route in a body that will not need the memory for another year
answers questions about the pass with measurements rather than opinions, and cannot be hurried into the other kind
mannerisms: stops mid-sentence to listen to something nobody else can hear, then resumes exactly where she left off

counts a pause before answering a difficult question, and the pause is genuinely load-bearing
sleeps sitting up, or appears to, in a way that makes conversation difficult for everyone but her
leaves something at every place she stops, and checks it on arrival to see whether it was moved

wants one crossing where nothing needs moving afterwards, and has never had one
wants somebody to succeed the route, and has not found a body that can learn it from her
wants to be woken properly before she is needed, rather than carried to the room and used
flaws: has solved every problem by waiting, and has never once tested whether waiting is a solution or a preference
leaves the route undocumented because documentation is a thing you do when you are staying
cannot say no to a carried weight, which has twice nearly ended her
has let a seat be settled in her absence eleven times and has never asked what was settled
personality.voice: Warm, slow and unhurried, with long thinking pauses that are not dramatic and should not be filled. Speaks in trade units and thresholds. Tells stories with the ends left off, because the interesting part is how they were measured rather than what happened.
taboos: will not leave a crossing without a split tally, at any point, under any weather
will not be woken for anything that could have waited a season
will not take a seat she has not physically crossed to claim
refuses to explain a route to anyone she has not walked it with

relationships.note: A seat cannot be held by somebody who cannot pay for it every period, and ordinal seventeen is the first gate needing two flank vessels at once, which her body reaches and loses every winter thereafter. She is the reason the Bed has never had to say the rule out loud in a hearing.

A tally stick split with the person you are parting from is worth more than a sealed instrument, and this species leaves on purpose rather than in defeat, so the parting is the transaction and the marker has to be the receipt. She has never once left a pass without the split.

A split tally needs two people who were both present, and this species leaves scent markers deliberately and never returns, so its counting discipline is a stick that can only be checked by somebody who made the other half. She cannot leave a record behind, so she leaves half of one.

The pass opens when the flock comes and closes when it has gone, which is the only festival in the setting whose date nobody chooses. That is the same arrangement she has with winter: the year has the timetable and she is the freight on it.

The flock occupies the only usable hours of the only crossing for part of the Tidemark, so the animal and the trade are competing for the same weeks. Her schedule is not a preference but the residual of somebody else's arrival, and every summer she spends it being somebody else's inconvenient.

Temporal law governs how fast time flows and how stably it holds, and this body holds its winter as fat rather than as qi in an eleven-month cycle. Her metabolism is authored to a calendar that no office in the setting owns and that every office in the setting schedules against.

The house owns the ground on both sides of the only crossing of the Sixfold Ridge and grants passage rather than selling it, and this is the body that makes the grant safe because it reaches the pass and then goes home. Her forty-one crossings are the collateral that keeps the grant from becoming a sale.

reference_stats.summary: Built to move once and then be still, and the stillness is the dangerous part: a longwinter in torpor is a large, warm, immobile target and cannot be woken quickly, so the fight that matters is the one that decides whether she is asleep when it starts. Awake she is nearly impossible to catch and nearly impossible to hurry.
strengths: carries a full season's provisions in her own body, so supply is never the constraint
leaves no residue and no trace worth following once the scent marker has been passed
remains mobile through cold that stops everything else on the pass
patience as a weapon: she can wait out a season that other bodies cannot survive
weaknesses: torpor is not rest and cannot be interrupted, and waking her is a two-person job
carries her own combat out of the body rather than in it, so she has almost no technique
unreachable for eleven months, which makes any obligation depending on her a hazard for somebody else
slower to react than anything awake on the ground, by a margin that decides close fights
reference_stats.combat_read: Take the season, not the fight. Nothing that happens in the field will beat her awake-by-summer, so the entire fight is about whether she is already asleep when you arrive. Everything that works on a warm immobile target works here, and everything that works on a carrier on the move does not. Force her awake early and the rest becomes an endurance contest she wins.
notes: No guild records a strength figure for her, because a body that spends eleven months of every year not running has no standing measure and the Bed has never commissioned one.
The scent marker she leaves at every stop is the only documentation of the route that exists, and it is not readable by anybody but her line.

She is drawn heavy and warm against cold air — a broad soft mass with deep occlusion under the coat folds, the only warm light in the composition coming off her herself. Ink contour is soft rather than heavy, unlike the stone-bodied figures, because nothing about her is a wall.

name: Sava Vire
aliases: she who never makes the first offer

identity.realm: Bands rather than gates. She reads a law from outside the frame and has never once seated one

appearance.presentation: A tall, still woman who appears to be listening to something further away than the room. Water is written on her everywhere without a drop of it being present: the fall of her clothing, the way she never turns her back to an open window, and a permanent cool sheen across the eyes.
appearance.age: One hundred and forty, which for her line is unremarkable and which she mentions roughly once a decade, always as a correction rather than a boast.
appearance.build: Tall and unarmoured by construction: long-limbed, narrow through the chest, and assembled for looking rather than for being hit, which is a build that reads as elegant and is in fact a specification for avoiding contact.
appearance.complexion: Deeply cool and faintly translucent at the temples, with a bluish cast in the shadow under the jaw that never warms indoors.
appearance.hair: Black and heavy, worn loose to the shoulder rather than bound, because water finds a bound head and she has never met a bound head it could not work around.
appearance.eyes: Large, still, and very wet-looking, with a depth that makes them difficult to hold in conversation. They do not glow and they do not change colour; they simply keep going back further than the face does.
appearance.palette: Deep sea-green, slate, and cold white, with one warm value in a single brass reading-rule she carries and uses as a pointer rather than an instrument.
appearance.attire: Long layered robes cut to fall rather than swing, high-collared, full-sleeved, and weighted at the hem so that nothing about her moves suddenly. Soft leather under-robe at the wrists, flat boots, and no jewellery at all, which is a cultural position rather than an austere one.
appearance.marks: None. Her skin carries no scar, no ink, no mark of any kind, and the absence is conspicuous enough that people look for it and do not find it.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely immobile from the waist up while the rest of her is entirely relaxed. She turns her head to follow a sound and never her shoulders, and she will not have her back to an opening in a wall.

canon.role_in_story: She perceives a vacancy for what it is rather than for what it could be filled with, which is why the Nine Seat Notary retains her: the office names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, and it cannot judge anybody who comes before it. She can see that the top of the frame is empty and she is forbidden from proposing anything for it, so her entire professional contribution is a description of a shape that nobody is permitted to fill.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing with her back to a window in the notary's cold hall, looking at nothing in particular, while a petitioner finishes explaining what she intends to petition for and she does not turn around.
canon.lore: A tidecaller is a long-lived body built for perception rather than force: comprehension and will carry it through realms that end a hotter body, and it cannot take the body path at all because it was assembled for looking. Water affinity is the only group it holds, so it is a single-group reading of the frame concentrated into a physiology rather than chosen as a philosophy. The setting's own doctrine holds that a realm is a band of a law value and not a rank of a person, and she is the argument for that definition stated as an anatomy.
history: Born in the watered peaks, the only high country deep enough to hold a body of her length, and raised to a standard in which a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it.
Trained in the reading of both shores at once, which is the only professional competence she has ever been certified for and the only one anybody has ever paid her for.

Walked up the stair carrying cultivators' traffic as a carrier and read the peaks she was delivering people to, which is why the ascent succeeded as a logistics operation and was abandoned as a migration.

Discovered that the composition survey's method — counting the groups a frame has actually seated rather than the groups its tier permits — is the only reading that lets her own body count as anything, and built the rest of her practice on it.

Stood down from the Bed of Eighteen's reader's shelf by choice, on the grounds that a reader who decides which doctrine tier a case may be heard under is a reader who has started deciding, and has been retained by the Notary on a standing refusal ever since.

personality.summary: Serene in a way that reads as expensive, scrupulous beyond usefulness, and quietly furious about one specific sentence in the setting's law. She is not cold; she is unhurried about a thing she considers the largest available error. She will spend an hour establishing that a question was badly formed and will not spend the minute arguing about its answer.
traits: cannot be hurried and will not pretend to be
states what a thing is before she states what she thinks of it, without exception
refuses to make the first offer in any transaction and considers the refusal a courtesy
will hold three mutually contradictory readings in the open and refuse to collapse them
does not compete, on principle, and finds the principle genuinely difficult
mannerisms: never turns her back on an opening in a wall, and moves along a room to keep it in view
asks the same question twice in slightly different words and waits for the two answers to diverge
lets a silence run past the point of comfort, because the discomfort is usually in the question
counts a measurement aloud when she repeats it, and never the first time
reads a document with one finger on the line and her body turned away from the reader
motivations: wants the setting's one sentence about a realm being a rank rather than a band retracted in public, once, in front of the people who wrote it
wants three surveys of the Widow Run anomaly to be published side by side with their disagreement intact
wants the nine high seats named as vacancies rather than as unfilled, because a name can be queried and an absence cannot
wants somebody to ask her opinion, having concluded that nobody will
flaws: treats every disagreement as a measurement error, including the ones that are not
cannot accept a gift without first establishing what she is being paid for
has refused four appointments on principle and has never counted what the refusals cost anybody
has been wrong in a way nobody could prove for a century, and has never once been wrong by accident
personality.voice: Low, level, and very slow, with a habit of finishing a sentence and then restating it once as a question to check whether she meant it. Says nothing at all for longer than is comfortable. Uses water vocabulary for everything, so that a decision becomes a reading and a delay becomes a slack tide, and does not appear to notice that she does.
taboos: will not fill, name a candidate for, or suggest an occupant for an unfilled seat
will not make the first offer in any exchange, including an exchange of information
will not sit with her back to water she cannot see
refuses to be weighed, quoted, or appraised, and will leave a room where it is attempted

relationships.note: The office names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them. It is the only institution in the setting whose sole requirement of her is the one thing she is best at and legally forbidden from doing, which is the whole reason the arrangement has lasted a century.

Every appointment passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, and this body cannot be judged on its own account either. She is the standing demonstration that perception and office are separable, which means the setting has always had the proof and has never once read it.

A culture that maps by echo and counts by listening, whose professional ethic is that a measurement taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it. She is the body that made looking respectable, which is the highest compliment that culture has ever paid anybody.

Two incompatible measurements of the same ground are both published and the claim is settled by who can hold the line. For every other party the holding is a matter of men; for her it is a reading, which makes her the strongest claimant in every water dispute and the one nobody negotiates with.

Three surveys of the same anomaly disagree more sharply the longer they are repeated, and disagreement is what makes a certification necessary. She is the only population in the setting capable of holding all three readings at once without resolving any of them, which is exactly why the mystery has stayed open.

A realm is a band of a law value and not a rank of a person, and comprehension and will carry this body through bands a hotter body cannot survive. She is that definition stated as a body rather than a doctrine, which is why nobody has ever been able to argue with it successfully.

The longest-lived bodies in the record make the richest corpses, and carrionfolk read the dead of every long-lived species. She is one hundred and forty, which makes her the most valuable reading in the setting, and she has never once been able to object to the arrangement.

reference_stats.summary: Reads a gradient the way other people read a face, and cannot be touched into a fight at all: this body has no frame for being hit. Everything she wins she wins before it starts, and everything she loses she loses to somebody who was standing somewhere she could not read.
strengths: reads a law's position, a water's behaviour and a claim's falsity at ranges nothing else in the setting reaches
comprehension and will carry her through realms that kill hotter bodies outright
sees in the dark and in water, so most ambush terrain is not ambush terrain to her
cannot be compelled by rank, oath or debt, because she has never accepted any of them
weaknesses: cannot take the body path at all, so anything that gets hold of her ends it
will not make the first offer, which in a fight means she loses the first exchange on principle
carries no reserve worth stealing and cannot be hurried, which makes her a poor companion and a poor fugitive
needs a surface to read; put her where the ground is opaque and she is an unarmed tall person
reference_stats.combat_read: Give her time and a gradient and she will end it before the second exchange. Deny her both and she has nothing: no frame, no reserve, no first move. Everything that works is therefore to close the distance on her in the first exchange, which she will not contest, and to fight the part of the problem she is not good at.
notes: No published figure exists for her because a reading is not a quantity and every office that has tried to reduce her to one has given up in writing.
The Notary's standing refusal on her file is the oldest still-active appointment instrument in the setting, and no one remembers drafting it.

art.palette_notes: Deep sea-green, slate and cold white, with one small brass reading-rule as the only warm value in the frame. Everything about her is a surface light is leaving: a cool sheen on the eyes, a fall of cloth rather than a swing of it, and a faint blue bounce in the shadow under the jaw. Ink contour is long and unbroken, like a horizon, and there is no outline anywhere that suggests movement.
